issues.legal_issue: The acquisition provision is not unconstitutional merely because it permits acquisition that deprives an owner of land.
material_facts: The acquisition was challenged as confiscatory and as violating constitutional protections concerning property and fundamental rights.
issues.conclusion: The constitutional challenge to Section 4 was rejected as wholly without substance.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Smt. Somavanti v. State of Punjab and Smt. Ratni Devi v. Chief Commissioner, Delhi, and held that the challenge failed under settled principles. It considered Article 144A unnecessary because the challenge had no merit.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges the constitutionality of a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.confiscatory_deprivation_claim: The challenger alleges that the acquisition provision is confiscatory and deprives the challenger of valuable land.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition challenge alleges confiscatory deprivation, the constitutional challenge is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A notice identifying land need not separately identify a superstructure standing on it.
material_facts: The acquisition notice specified the land but did not separately mention the superstructure standing on it.
The statutory definition of land included any superstructure on the land.
issues.conclusion: The omission of a separate description of the superstructure did not invalidate the notice.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(a) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the definition of land includes a superstructure on it; the law did not require the structure to be separately mentioned in the notice.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.notice_identifies_land: The acquisition notice identifies the land proposed to be acquired.
predicates.existing_structure_not_separately_identi: A structure exists on the identified land but is not separately described in the notice.

issues.definition: If a challenged acquisition notice identifies the land but does not separately describe a structure on it, the notice is not invalid for that omission.

issues.legal_issue: Land acquired for staff quarters serving a public scheme may be acquired for a public purpose.
material_facts: The proposed staff quarters were for employees working under the Employees' State Insurance Scheme.
The Court found the quarters closely connected with the scheme's operation and implementation.
issues.conclusion: Acquisition for the staff quarters was for a public purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, under which the declaration is conclusive evidence that the land is needed for a public purpose, and relied on Smt. Somavanti v. State of Punjab. It also held that staff quarters serving the scheme were themselves a public purpose.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.staff_housing_serves_public_scheme: The proposed staff housing is for employees whose work serves the public scheme for which the land is acquired.

issues.definition: When staff housing in a challenged acquisition serves the relevant public scheme, the acquisition is for a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A dispute over whether scheme funds may be spent on staff quarters does not invalidate an acquisition that is otherwise for a public purpose.
material_facts: The challenge asserted that the statutory provisions governing the scheme's funds did not authorize expenditure on staff quarters.

The Court found the quarters connected with the operation and implementation of the scheme and held that the relevant fund could be used for that purpose under specified clauses or with special authorization.
The Court added that even if the expenditure were not strictly authorized, that would not invalidate an acquisition whose purpose was otherwise public.
issues.conclusion: The objection based on the scheme's expenditure provisions did not invalidate the acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 28(i), (iv) and (xii) of the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, and held that, even assuming the expenditure was not strictly authorized, that would not defeat an acquisition for an otherwise public purpose.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.staff_quarters_connected_to_scheme: The proposed staff quarters are connected with the operation and implementation of the scheme they serve.
predicates.acquisition_has_public_purpose: The acquisition is otherwise for a public purpose.

issues.definition: If staff quarters are connected to the scheme and the acquisition has a public purpose, an objection about whether scheme funds may pay for the quarters does not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: General statutory notice of a proposed acquisition is sufficient where the rules do not require special individual notice.
material_facts: The challengers did not dispute compliance with the requirements to publish the notice in the Official Gazette and give public notice of its substance at convenient places in the locality.
The rule relied on by the challengers did not impose a further special-notice requirement.
issues.conclusion: No special notice to the challengers was required.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, requires publication in the Official Gazette and public notice of the substance of the notification at convenient places in the locality. Rule 30B of the Gujarat Land Acquisition Rules did not add a requirement for special individual notice.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.general_notice_given: The substance of the proposed acquisition is publicly notified through the required general methods.
predicates.no_rule_requires_special_notice: The applicable rule does not require a separate special notice to the challenger.

issues.definition: When the required general notice is given and no applicable rule calls for special notice, individual special notice is not required.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner need not receive a further hearing after the officer has completed the objections inquiry and submitted the report to the government.
material_facts: The challengers had filed objections and received a full opportunity to present them in the inquiry.
The officer submitted a report to the government, after which the government considered the report and proceeded with the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The law did not require a further opportunity to make submissions after the report was submitted to the government.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 5A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and held that the government considers the officer's report and decides how to proceed; there is no additional hearing requirement after the report. It relied on State of Gujarat v. Ambalal Haiderbhai for the principle that an inquiry, whether administrative or judicial, must comply with natural justice.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and objections_inquired_into and objectors_given_full_opportunity and report_submitted_to_government

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.objections_inquired_into: An officer conducts an inquiry into the objections to the acquisition.
predicates.objectors_given_full_opportunity: The objectors receive a full opportunity to present their objections during the inquiry.
predicates.report_submitted_to_government: The officer submits the inquiry report to the government for consideration.

issues.definition: If objections have been inquired into after a full opportunity to the objectors and the report has been submitted to the government, no further hearing after the report is required.

issues.legal_issue: A declaration is not invalid on the ground that an unauthorized officer made the objections report when an appointed collector heard the objections and submitted the report.
material_facts: A person appointed as a collector under the Act heard the objections and made a report to the government.
The matter was later transferred to another officer, but nothing effective or substantial was done by that officer before the declaration.
The government considered the appointed collector's report when issuing the declaration.
issues.conclusion: There was no infirmity in the declaration based on the report, because the appointed collector had heard the objections and made the report considered by the government.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3(c), 5A and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the objections inquiry and report could be made by an officer appointed as a collector; the declaration was not invalid where that officer had dealt with the objections and the government considered the report.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and objections_heard_by_appointed_collector and appointed_collector_submitted_report and declaration_considered_report

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.objections_heard_by_appointed_collector: An officer appointed as a collector hears the objections to the acquisition.
predicates.appointed_collector_submitted_report: The appointed collector submits the report on the objections to the government.
predicates.declaration_considered_report: The government considers that report before issuing the acquisition declaration.

issues.definition: If an appointed collector hears the objections and submits a report that the government considers, the declaration is not invalid because of a later claim that the report lacked proper authority.

issues.legal_issue: A claim that acquired land was used as a burial ground fails where the evidence does not establish that use.
material_facts: The High Court found that the land was not being used as a burial ground.
The evidence described two old, dilapidated tombs in a corner of a larger area, while the remainder was open, unused and uncared for; some parts were used to prepare cow-dung cakes.
The Supreme Court found no sufficient ground to differ from the High Court's conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the burial-ground objection and declined to disturb the High Court's finding.
issues.legal_principle: The Court resolved the objection on the factual record and found no sufficient basis to overturn the High Court's finding that the land was not being used as a burial ground.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.burial_ground_objection: The challenger asserts that the land is being used as a burial ground.
predicates.land_not_actually_used_as_burial_ground: The evidence shows that the land is not actually being used as a burial ground.

issues.definition: When a burial-ground objection is raised in an acquisition challenge but the land is not actually used as a burial ground, the objection is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A small contribution from the public exchequer does not make an acquisition for a public body's use invalid.
material_facts: The acquisition was for the use of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation.
The challengers argued that the small contribution from the public exchequer was a colourable exercise of power and did not satisfy the statutory requirement.
issues.conclusion: The objection to the amount of the public contribution was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the majority decision in Smt. Somavanti v. State of Punjab and on Inderjit Parekh v. State of Gujarat in rejecting the contention that the limited public contribution defeated the acquisition.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A party challenges a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.land_acquired_for_public_body_use: The land is acquired for the use of a public body.
predicates.public_exchequer_makes_contribution: The public exchequer contributes toward the acquisition.

issues.definition: If land is acquired for a public body's use and the public exchequer contributes, the limited size of that contribution does not invalidate the acquisition.
